title: Maximal quantum leakage: operational interpretation and quantum channel analysis
authors: Shuixin Xiao, Zijia Zhao, Jingge Zhu, Farhad Farokhi
abstract: Maximal quantum leakage quantifies privacy against adversaries with arbitrary intentions. In this work, we prove that computing this leakage is equivalent to minimum-error quantum state discrimination with equal priors. This establishes a computable operational interpretation, addressing the previous difficulty in computing maximal quantum leakage. We further analyze the impact of collective measurements on multiple copies of a state, demonstrating that leakage increases monotonically with the number of copies, which leads to explicitly characterizing the maximal leakage in the asymptotic limit. Extending this framework to quantum channels, we develop an iterative algorithm for the jointly designing of input states and measurements. Numerical examples involving collective measurements and the maximal channel leakage demonstrate our theoretical findings.
summary: This work establishes a computable operational definition for maximal quantum leakage by proving its equivalence to minimum-error state discrimination. The authors develop an iterative algorithm to calculate this leakage when considering noisy quantum channels. This advances the field by providing concrete mathematical tools to quantify information privacy in quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide a computable operational interpretation for quantifying 'maximal quantum leakage,' which measures privacy when classical data is encoded into a quantum system.
main_result: Maximal quantum leakage has been proven equivalent to minimum-error quantum state discrimination with equal priors, allowing it to be formulated as a solvable Semidefinite Programming (SDP) problem.
method: The authors establish the equivalence via mathematical proofs and develop an iterative algorithm that alternates optimization between input states and measurements for channel analysis.
model_or_system: The study operates within quantum information theory, analyzing leakage quantified by POVMs, quantum channels ($\mathcal{E}$), and ensembles of quantum states $\{ho_x\}$.
key_observables: Maximal Quantum Leakage ($Q(X 	o A)$), minimum-error discrimination probability.
important_parameters: Number of copies ($n$), number of distinct inputs ($N=|X|$), dimension of the Hilbert space ($d$).
main_assumptions: The equivalence proof relies on constructing optimal measurement sets from arbitrary POVMs; the iterative algorithm is proposed for non-convex optimization.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the monotonic increase of leakage with copies towards a limit. Figure 2 illustrates the convergence of the iterative algorithm for channel leakage over multiple steps.
paper_structure: The paper first defines maximal quantum leakage, proves its equivalence to minimum-error state discrimination (Theorem 1), analyzes its behavior for collective measurements (monotonicity and asymptotic limits), and finally extends the framework to develop an iterative algorithm for quantifying leakage through quantum channels.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous mathematical tools (SDP formulation) to quantify information leakage in quantum systems, which is crucial for secure quantum communication protocols and understanding channel capacity limitations.
